correctness.rationale: Independently rebuilt the zero-sum powered-distance quadratic form on the hub, two leaf-population means and within-class zero-mean fluctuations. Two strictly negative fluctuation sectors and the 2x2 mean block M_p yield det(M_p)=mn(ab)^p[F_mF_n-mn Δ_p²]. For 1<p<min(P_m,P_n), F_m,F_n decrease and Δ_p>0 strictly increases (numerator 1-u^p-(1-u)^p grows and denominator falls). The determinant changes from positive at 1 to negative at min P, giving a unique root. Weighted tree strict 1-negative type and strict lower-exponent inheritance cover p<=1; at root nullity one and above it the form fails, giving snowflake ranks m+n and m+n-1. For contrast, log-sinh concavity proves Δ_p(e^s,e^-s) decreases as s grows for 1<p<2, so the root rises to P_max, whereas equal lengths give P_{m+n}. A direct independent full metric distance-matrix and centered Gram calculation verified roots and ranks for (m,n,a,b)=(2,2,1,3),(3,6,1,1),(4,7,0.12,10): roots 1.427217382226, 1.169925001442, 1.184975971877, each endpoint corank1. The proof covers arbitrary finite positive ratio, unlike numeric samples.

The 1990 Deza–Maehara metric transform paper remains a primary full-text access risk, not an automatic rejection.
